name: Earlham Institute DNA Foundry (BBSRC-funded automated DNA fabrication facility, 2016)
brief: An academic DNA foundry for synthetic biology: acoustic liquid handling for nanolitre DNA assembly, robotic transformation and plating, colony picking and arraying, automated DNA purification and quantification, gel electrophoresis and microfermentation screening, offered as a service to academic and industrial users.

cost.excludes_note: Source says 'Funded by a GBP 1.9M grant' to provide DNA fabrication facilities; it does not itemise equipment versus staff or running costs. USD at about 1.30-1.40 USD/GBP (2016), an assumption.

notes: Kept unverified: the grant amount is confirmed but no source says what it paid for, so it cannot be compared like-for-like. Verified 3 Oct 2026, Earlham press release 23 Aug 2016: "Funded by a GBP 1.9M grant, led by EI's Head of Platforms & Pipelines Dr Daniel Swan, the EI DNA Foundry is one of five locations funded by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC) to provide the UK's academic community and synthetic biology industries with DNA fabrication facilities." Equipment list is from the CURRENT biofoundry page (2026), which includes later additions (Opentrons Flex, BioLector XT), so it does not match what the 2016 grant bought; treat the mapping as indicative. Grant coverage unknown (includes left empty).
